title: When the Ferry Goes Your Way

plate.narration: At Ashspan Bridge, river water taps the ferry landing. A flat boat waits beside its long pole. The road crosses overhead, while the current carries on toward the coast.

goal.text: Lend a hand at the river ferry before you go on.

bridge.narration: The bridge over the Great River is called Ashspan Bridge. Old Ossley, a frogfolk boatman, rests a pole across his flat boat. "Changed melt," he says, watching a branch turn in the current. "Busy year." You can help the waiting travelers board. A raised footpath leads to a village in the Whispering Marsh. "There is a school called the Academy there," he says. "They teach a class called Starweaver. Those heroes read the stars. If you visit, could you bring back the dry reed mat they made for my deck? Follow the posts. The ducks take shortcuts. You should not."

variants.text: He checks the blanket around your shoulders before returning to his pole.

landing.narration: A mooring rope has dragged a landing plank loose. Ossley is holding the boat steady while two travelers wait with their bags. What will you do?

choices.label: Hold the plank while the travelers board
Help move the rope off the plank

plank.narration: You hold the plank flat until both travelers are aboard. Ossley tests it once with his pole and nods. "That will do."

choices.label: Visit the Academy in the marsh
Stay at the ferry and discuss the roads

rope.narration: You lift the rope clear and seat the plank on its supports. The travelers board without wetting their bags. Ossley gives you a brief nod.

choices.label: Visit the Academy in the marsh
Stay at the ferry and discuss the roads

routes.narration: Ossley points downriver. "The coast is called the Saltrot. When I go." Then he points to the road beside the boundary stones. You can ask about the coast or follow the stone-keepers' questions inland. For now, you have a safe landing and a route to discuss. He marks an upper bank road north to a landing called Frostfang Shore. "Dry ground. Long walk. Griffin country at the far end."

marsh_path.narration: The raised path carries you into the Whispering Marsh. Reeds brush your sleeves. Ahead, a village stands on wooden legs above the water. A rolled reed mat waits beside a notice: "For the ferry. Please keep dry." A puddle fills the last stretch of path. How will you carry the mat back?

choices.label: Carry it high above the puddle
Wrap it in your dry cloak

mat_high.narration: You lift the mat overhead and carry it to a dry bench in the village. A duck walks under it. For a moment, the duck has a roof.

mat_wrap.narration: You wrap the mat in a dry cloak and carry it to a bench in the village. Water splashes your ankles. The mat stays dry. Your socks are less lucky.

village_rest.narration: You rest beside the dry mat in the marsh village. A round tower rises above the reeds. It has no roof. A page of homework floats down and lands on a duck. The duck looks pleased with its marks. The posted path will take you back to the ferry.

choices.label: Climb the tower with no roof
Carry the mat back to the ferry

mat_return.narration: You follow the posts out of the marsh and back to the bridge. Ossley unrolls the dry mat across his wet deck. The travelers step onto it without slipping. "Better," he says. He tucks a corner under a rope so it will stay put.

academy.narration: Above the marsh village, at the top of the tower is a classroom with no roof at all, only sky. This school is called the Academy. Here students learn to be a Starweaver, a hero who reads the stars. A dragonling named Professor Nettle stands beside a huge brass telescope. Homework floats up off the desks and drifts away over the reeds. Nobody chases it. "It comes down somewhere," says the professor. On a cushion sits a star circlet. A Starweaver's light lives in that circlet, and a dusk hood worn beside it starts to itch. "Anyone who wants the circlet," says Professor Nettle, "may try it on."

variants.text: Professor Nettle waves from beside the big brass telescope. "Back at the Academy! Mind the homework." A page floats past your nose and off over the reeds. The star circlet waits on its cushion for anyone who wants to try it on.

academy_stars.narration: Professor Nettle lets you look through the telescope. Even by day, the stars are so close you could count their points. Then the telescope sneezes. Brass rattles. Dust puffs out of the far end. "Bless you," says the professor, to the telescope. "It does that when it sees something new."

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
